requirements.title: When dedicated governance expertise is essential
requirements.body: The AI Act imposes layered requirements that cut across law, technology, and operations. An AI Officer ensures your company has a professional accountable for interpretation, implementation, and communication—helping to avoid fragmented responsibility and late-stage compliance surprises.
requirements.helper: Need a single point of expertise?

items.title: High-Risk AI System Providers
items.description: Developers of Annex III systems need structured risk management, documentation, and authority-facing processes.
examples: Safety-related components in transport or energy
HR recruitment and educational AI tools

items.title: General-Purpose AI / Foundation Model Developers
items.description: Providers of large models face transparency, systemic risk, and data governance expectations.
examples: API providers offering generative AI services

items.title: AI Deployers & Integrators
items.description: Businesses using AI must ensure human oversight, monitor system performance, and contract responsibly with vendors.
examples: Banks using AI for credit scoring
Public sector agencies using AI for services
Enterprises integrating AI features into workflows

factsIntro.title: AI Act compliance is ongoing governance
factsIntro.body: The AI Act is not a one-off project—it requires continuous governance. An AI Officer provides structure: documenting obligations, reviewing third-party tools, addressing IP and licensing, and ensuring compliance is integrated into everyday development and operations.
